prompt: Challenge C061-CH1: Our cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil goes rancid within 4 months on shelf, but competitors manage 9–12 months; we lose about 15% of each batch

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Photo-oxidative degradation pathways in oils are strongly light-dependent, with UV-A radiation causing lutein half-life loss six times faster than fluorescent light and substantially accelerating lipid co-oxidation measured by peroxide value increase.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-06406","field":"abstract","quote":"Under UV-A, lutein half-life was 11.3 h compared to 38.7 h under fluorescent light. Peroxide value increased sixfold faster under UV-A."}]},{"text":"Polyunsaturated fatty acid content in carrier oils drives photo-oxidative degradation rates; cold-pressed hemp seed oil showed photodegradation rate constants 4.1 times higher than saturated medium-chain triglyceride oil, with lipid oxidation directly correlated to carotenoid loss.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-06409","field":"abstract","quote":"β-Carotene photodegradation rate constants were 0.031, 0.012, and 0.049 h⁻¹ for sunflower, MCT, and hemp seed oil emulsions, respectively. The markedly higher rate in hemp seed emulsions correlated with faster peroxide value increases"}]},{"text":"Modest antioxidant supplementation such as 0.05% tocopherol can extend UV-A half-life by 69% and suppress secondary oxidation markers by 34%, indicating that tocopherol content analysis should be prioritized for understanding why current rosemary extract trials failed.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-06406","field":"abstract","quote":"Addition of 0.05 % tocopherol to the oil phase extended UV-A half-life to 19.1 h and suppressed malondialdehyde formation by 34 %."}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher's expertise directly addresses the challenge's core problem: determining which oxidation pathway—photo-oxidative versus other mechanisms—is driving peroxide value increase in cold-pressed oil, and quantifying how light exposure and fatty acid composition control degradation kinetics [SYN-PUB-06406, SYN-PUB-06409] without requiring gas chromatography, while evaluating why natural antioxidants like tocopherol matter more than plant extracts [SYN-PUB-06406]."}
